title: I made a free LucasArts-style point & click about Bilbo's birthday party, using AI for the art (Claude + GPT images)
author: XRylynX
selftext:
Hi! I'm a solo hobbyist dev from Spain and I just released Bilbo's Pocket 1.0, a free, non-profit Tolkien fan tribute in the style of the classic 90s LucasArts adventures (verbs, inventory, dialogue trees).

How it was made:

\- All backgrounds, portraits and sprites started as AI images (GPT image gen), then cleaned up and pixel-adjusted.

\- Code, dialogue system and tooling were built together with Claude.

\- The writing, story design and canon-checking against The Fellowship of the Ring are mine. Every quote in the game is taken word for word from the book.

\- Original music, full English/Spanish versions, playable in the browser.

\- The fireworks clip above was animated from the game art with Seedance.

The hardest part was keeping characters consistent across scenes and making walk cycles that don't look AI-weird. Happy to share the workflow if anyone's interested.

Play free in your browser: https://rylyncot.itch.io/el-bolsillo-de-bilbo

Feedback very welcome!

comments.author: MakingSoulStudio
comments.body: The sprites are really well made. It feels like stepping inside a page of a storybook.

replies.author: XRylynX
replies.body: Thanks! Lots of work and trial/error till I was satisfied 😀

replies.author: MakingSoulStudio
replies.body: You can really tell how much work you put in. Rooting for you!

replies.author: XRylynX
replies.body: The trickiest part was the walk cycles: AI kept giving me hobbits with extra legs, so I ended up drawing simple stick-figure guides for each frame and redoing them until they felt right

comments.author: novokvest
comments.body: Hi! I've actually seen your game on itch already but haven't played yet, I'll try when I have more time and report back. But I'm very curious at your experience making it. I don't own claude subsctiption so I don't know how much it helps for point and click adventure games. Like does it understand 2D rooms layout? Can it autotest it? I've seen others made point and clicks primarily with Claude. How crucial was it for you?

replies.author: XRylynX
replies.body:
Thanks! Honestly, Claude was crucial. My programming skills are very basic, so without it the game simply wouldn't exist. It wrote basically all the engine: verbs, inventory, dialogue trees, save system, cutscenes, the English/Spanish switch.

About your questions:
- 2D room layout: it doesn't "see" the room by itself, but if you give it the background image it can look at it and help you define walkable areas (polygons), hotspots and depth scaling. Then you tweak by hand.
- Testing: it can run the game in a browser, take screenshots and check if something looks wrong, which saves a lot of time. Puzzle logic still needs a human playthrough though.
- What it can't do well: art consistency and animations. Walk cycles were the hardest part; I ended up drawing simple stick-figure guides for each frame so the image AI kept the proportions.

My advice: keep each session focused on one scene or one system, and keep notes of what's done, because long projects get messy fast. Hope you enjoy the game when you try it!

replies.author: novokvest
replies.body: Yeah, maybe on weekends. I get it now, thanks. I mean if we have an existing engine it would be a very different thing. In point and clicks that I made there's not that many code, basically only switch inventory logic and dialog scripts. So as of now there is no one prompt "make me a pac about Bilbo". But as I follow pacs made with AI on itch for quite a while there has been notisable boom of new demos in past months.
